text:
maria: quick follow-up on the KV cache RFC — specifically prefix caching eviction & sharing. want to align on correctness guarantees before we ship.

chen: thanks. what are you worried about exactly? eviction order? cross-tenant sharing?

maria: both. main tradeoffs: strict per-session prefix isolation vs aggressive sharing for perf. also eviction strategy (LRU vs TTL vs weighted) affects consistency when we rely on stale KV states for next-token generation.

ryan: my take: safety-first. if a cached prefix can change logits for an in-flight generation, we need pinning or versioned keys. otherwise we risk serving inconsistent continuations.

olivia: agree. propose we attach a cache-version to each model-serving config and include that in keys. when model or tokenizer changes, bump version -> implicit invalidation.

maria: that helps model-level correctness but not sharing across sessions with different prompt prefixes. think about multi-user prefix reuse (e.g., same system prompt): we want to share KV to save compute.

chen: maybe a two-tier key: <model>@<cache-version>#<prefix-id>. prefix-id can be a content-hash for shared prefixes or a session-id for private ones. that keeps sharing explicit.

ryan: eviction: prefer a hybrid of TTL + size-based LRU. TTL avoids hot stale entries and LRU bounds memory. but need to ensure we never evict pinned keys used by in-flight requests.

olivia: pinned keys => tracked per-worker inflight map. workers increment pin_count when starting generation and decrement on finish. eviction ignores pin_count>0.

maria: implementation detail: do we store pin_count in shared redis or local worker mem? redis gives global correctness but adds latency on every pin/unpin.

chen: idea: local pin_count + lease heartbeat to controller. controller periodically reconciles. avoids sync overhead for high QPS while still preventing long-lived pins from being lost.

ryan: tests: we'll need unit tests for race between eviction and pin/unpin, plus an integration test with simulated worker crashes to ensure leases expire and keys become evictable.

olivia: rollout plan: default to per-tenant isolated prefixes for 2 weeks, flip opt-in flag for shared-prefix-cache behind feature gate, monitor perplexity/regression metrics and token-level deltas.

maria: + add metrics: cache_hit_rate by prefix-type, eviction_reclaims, pinned_eviction_attempts, lease_expirations. tie alerts if hit_rate drops or eviction attempts spike.

chen: I'll draft follow-up PR with config snippet and test plan. snippet for keys & eviction config:

```
cache:
  key_format: "{model}:{version}#{prefix_type}:{prefix_hash}"
  eviction:
    policy: "ttl+lru"
    ttl_seconds: 3600
    max_entries: 500000
  pinning:
    mode: "local_with_lease"
    lease_seconds: 30
```

maria: perfect. please include migration notes for Dedicated/Private customers – they may want stricter isolation. cc @infra-bot for infra implications.

infra-bot: noted. will add capacity and redis keyspace recommendations to the infra playbook.

ryan: one more thing — document fallback behavior: if prefix missing, runtime recomputes and repopulates. ensure we log origin (miss/recompute) for debugging.

maria: excellent. thanks everyone. chen, assign the RFC follow-up to eng-runtime board when ready.
